topic: Mastering Putnam Competition Problem-Solving: The Art of Symmetry and Invariants
target_audience: University students with a strong background in competition mathematics

sections.title: Introduction: The Putnam Mindset (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Putnam problems demand creative, first-principle thinking.
Invariants remain unchanged despite system evolution.
Consider a chameleon moving on a checkerboard.
Parity shows the square's color invariant.
This core concept drives Putnam problem-solving.
animations: Display title "The Putnam Mindset" in white #FFFFFF.
Fade in a light bulb icon representing creative problem solving.
Animate a maze path finding its way out.
Final transition showing the path to the solution.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Discrete vs. Continuous Invariants (0:45-1:45)
lecture_lines: Categorize tools into discrete and continuous.
Use parity and modular arithmetic for discrete.
Use monotone functions or potentials for continuous.
animations: Show discrete set of points in #00FFFF.
Animate transition of points converging to a line.

sections.title: Core Strategy: Exploiting Symmetry (1:45-3:15)
lecture_lines: Exploit symmetry to simplify complex systems.
Symmetry reduces search space for solutions.
Check centroids when systems show rotational symmetry.
Set variables equal to solve algebraic complexity.
Symmetry is a powerful reduction technique.
animations: Reflect the shape across an axis in #FF0000.
Overlay both operations to show invariance.

sections.title: Application: The Pigeonhole Principle & Extremal Method (3:15-4:30)
lecture_lines: Combine invariants with the Extremal Principle.
Focus on the largest or smallest element.
Extremal values create contradictions or base cases.
animations: Show 5 pigeonholes in #FFFFFF and 6 pigeons in #FF0000.
Highlight the pigeon without a hole in #00FF00.

sections.title: Conclusion: Developing Your Toolkit (4:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Analyze symmetry to unlock the problem.
Identify invariants to track system state.
Apply the extremal principle to conclude.
